items.title: Butch Miles interviewed by Monk Rowe and Michael Woods, Scottsdale, Arizona, March 4, 1995 [interview 1 of 2]
items.q: I was with Dave Brubeck part of a year, and just had such a wonderful time with his quartet. As a matter of fact when I left the Basie band I went right with the Brubeck quartet.

ctx.x: Since the Basie band, what have been some of your favorite moments?

Oh, gee, it’s a lot of them, I’ve got to tell you, because I left the band 16 years ago, in 1979. I hadn’t thought about that. But since then I’ve gone and traveled all over the world, I’ve worked with a lot of great different people. It was funny I never had a chance to work with Sweets Edison until after I left the band, you know, and then I started from time to time working with ex-Basieites, we kind of like would conglomerate and get together, Clark Terry, the magnificent Red Holloway, I was with Dave Brubeck…
Can I ask you a question? Did you play a show with Dave Brubeck in Tulsa, Oklahoma —

items.title: Butch Miles interviewed by Monk Rowe, via Zoom, October 9, 2020 [interview 2 of 2]
items.q: I joined up with Dave Brubeck’s quartet.

ctx.x: Okay. Do you feel your playing has changed over the years either out of necessity or out of choice?

Yes, yes and yes. It has changed over the years. And some of it has been out of necessity because I had worked for the first four and a half years where I — for wont of a better phrase — made my bones, I was working with the Basie band. And that’s where I got my reputation. Then the next thing I turned around, as you remember, and I joined up with Dave Brubeck’s quartet. (How could he do that?) Well it was easy for me because I was raised on both Basie and Brubeck. Then later I started playing with other groups,…

that were of a different type of, oh I don’t know what the word would be, a connotation for a musical genre or a style, and I found that I just couldn’t stay in one particular crevice, a musical crevice as it were. I couldn’t apply what I’ve always been playing to (A) when the band was playing let’s say (B) I had to think of something else to play. So I would have to switch and it got me to thinking and got me to changing my style because I had to. And then later on I found that there was so much enjoyment in…
